channel.title: Cato Institute – Bias and Credibility - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Cato Institute – Bias and Credibility (cato.org)

item.title: Obamacare at 16: There's No Reason Not to Provide Consumers Relief
item.description: The arguments against Obamacare relief do not comport with the available evidence.

item.title: The Remedy-Free Zone: Reclaiming State Power to Curb Federal Misconduct
item.description: State-law remedies merely provide a way to enforce existing federal rights; an unconstitutional act is, by definition, outside the scope of lawful authority.

item.title: No, Credit Card Interest Rate Caps Won't Help Consumers
item.description: We do not live in a simple world where the intent behind a law magically prevents unintended consequences. Luckily, we do live in a world where we know the downside of interest rate caps.

item.title: Postal Service Out of Cash
item.description: The best reform would be for Congress to privatize the USPS and give company managers the flexibility to make reforms based on cost factors and consumer demands.

item.title: Rare Earths, Vulcan, and Government Equity Stakes
item.description: While the US has strategic supply chain concerns, federal ownership of private companies is both unnecessary and undesirable.

item.title: Congress Hasn’t Funded TSA’s Paychecks and That Should Matter
item.description: If we can no longer be confident that Congress could constrain the president through its purse strings, the Constitution’s remaining checks and balances may be too weak to function as the liberty-preserving structural safeguards on which we depend.

item.title: Reconciliation 2.0 Should Put Housing Supply First
item.description: If lawmakers want a serious, growth-oriented affordability agenda, housing supply must be central, and cost recovery reform should take center stage.

item.title: How the American Healthcare System Rewards Psychiatric Overdiagnosis
item.description: Why the surge in diagnoses may say more about incentives than illness.

item.title: Curtailing Religious Liberties at Maryland Private Schools Is No April Fool’s Day Prank
item.description: A Maryland bill that could restrict religious liberty at private schools is the latest evidence that supporters of educational freedom must always be vigilant—with or without school choice funding.

item.title: From FBI Assessment to FISA §702 Query: AI-Assisted Predicate Laundering
item.description: The absence of a warrant requirement leaves the constitutional protection of US persons entirely dependent on executive branch oversight that has been systematically removed.

item.title: CBDCs Can’t Give You Everything, Everywhere, All at Once
item.description: At best, this list showcases extreme optimism in the efficacy of government programs. At worst, this list borders on false advertising.

item.title: The Supreme Court Should Affirm Birthright Citizenship
item.description: The original meaning of the Fourteenth Amendment is incompatible with President Trump’s order purporting to end birthright citizenship.

item.title: A Few Key Points on Trump's New Elections Executive Order
item.description: Trump is clearly frustrated with Congress’s inability to pass new election laws. He doesn’t interpret this as a mandate to go back to the legislative drawing board, but rather a license to legislate without Congress or without the states.

item.title: Prevent the Next TSA Crisis, Privatize Airport Screening
item.description: There is a better strategy Congress can pursue: privatize security screening at the nation’s airports.

item.title: Who Owns Digital Records—Tech Companies or Their Users? In Chatrie v. US, the Supreme Court Could Weigh In
item.description: Several amici briefs, including ours, explored the important Fourth Amendment question in Chatrie: Who owns the digital records a person creates—the customer? Or Google, which stores the Location History records?
